newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia test fires Ballistic missile. [CORRECTED 09:30 GMT 10/11]
newsitem.headline: Russia test fires Ballistic missile. [CORRECTED 09:30 GMT 10/11]

text.p: (Corrects headline to show the missile was a Ballistic missile and not a Cruise missile.)
Russia successfully test fired an RS-12M Topol (Poplar) intercontinental ballistic missile on Saturday from the Plesetsk test site in the far north, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Tass quoted the Strategic Missile Forces commander, General Igor Sergeyev, as saying that the servicemen who had launched the missile had "demonstrated irreproachable training and professionalism".
"The launch showed again the high combat training of the troops and the reliability and technical readiness of the interballistic missiles of this class," Tass quoted Sergeyev as saying.
Russia has yet to ratify the START-2 strategic arms reduction treaty with Washington which would slash U.S. and Russian warheads to about 3,000 on each side by 2003.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry travelled to Moscow last month trying to persuade the State Duma lower house of parliament to approve the treaty, ratified by the U.S. Senate earlier this year.
The Duma, dominated by President Boris Yeltsin's opponents and deeply suspicious of planned NATO expansion into eastern Europe, appeared to be unconvinced.
